newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FORECAST - Trelleborg '96 profit seen lower.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Trelleborg '96 profit seen lower.

text.p: Swedish mining and rubber company Trelleborg was expected to post a lower profit after financial items of 1.02 billion crowns for full year 1996, a Reuters poll of eight analysts found.
This would be a fall of 71 percent on a year earlier when Trelleborg posted a profit after financial items of 3.51 billion crowns including restructuring costs of 1.97 billion crowns.
Forecasts for 1996 varied between 980 million and 1.05 billion crowns with a mean of 1.02 billion crowns.
The company itself forecast in its nine month report that its year profit would be about a billion crowns.
Trelleborg was forecast to increase its dividend payment to 3.50 crowns from 3.00 crowns in 1995.
For calendar 1997 and 1998 analysts forecast full year profits of 1.17 billion crowns and 1.50 billion crowns respectively.
Many analysts believed the situation regarding Trelleborg's base metal business would become clear in the coming year.

"We will probably get to see continuing pressure on copper prices this year but I think the stronger dollar and mainly higher zinc prices will more than neutralise this," said one of the more optimistic analysts.
Another analyst also said metal prices were uncertain but added that the dollar was clearly a positive factor.
"I have enough to justify a higher profit forecast for 1997 and 1998 on the ground of the stronger dollar," he said.
Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Swedbank, Fiba Nordic, Kleinwort Benson, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Paribas, Alfred Berg, Nordbanken, and Carnegie.
Trelleborg is due to release its 1996 results around midday.
